acts.title: The Ornament
acts.goal: Bring Val back into the Cole mansion, plant the letters and the star, and end on the first proof that the past was stolen.

acts.title: The Trap
acts.goal: Let Eleanor use the wedding and the prenup to tighten the trap while Nate and Val trace the letters to Walter.

acts.title: The First Crack
acts.goal: Move the wedding to Christmas Eve, expose the forged letter, and make Eleanor decide to burn the tin.

acts.title: The Dark Night
acts.goal: Break Walter open, put the tin in Nate's hands, and make Eleanor disown the truth in public.

acts.title: The Turn
acts.goal: Expose the prenup, interrupt the wedding, and turn the letters into public evidence.
acts.cliffhanger: YOU CAME BACK FOR A BOX

acts.title: The Payoff
acts.goal: Expel Val, rescue the tin from the furnace, race the midnight train, and pay off the star and the opening line.

source_script: Proven adaptation beat map (La Lavandera del Rancho, 22-block structure, Christmas surface): B1 Val decorates the Cole mansion; Nate arrives with Madison; the crystal star ornament; Eleanor freezes. B2 Eleanor keeps a letter in the red cookie tin; June sees; Walter keeps one letter; the audience learns the secret. B3 Eleanor keeps Val close to humiliate her; June becomes Val's ally. B4 Nate hears the sailor lie; Val tells him the letters existed. B5 Nate sees Val's star signature; Madison recognizes it; Walter cracks. B6 Nate and Val trace the mail route to Walter; Nate stands beside Val in public. B7 Eleanor burns a letter; June saves a charred star; the Christmas Eve wedding is marked. B8 Nate finds an old Christmas photograph and admits he never stopped loving Val. B9 Eleanor moves the wedding to Christmas Eve; Val sees the prenup; Nate asks for one night. B10 June gives Val the cellar key; Val finds Walter's stolen letter; Eleanor traps her with the tin. B11 Eleanor shows Nate the fake letter; Val sees the missing star; Eleanor orders the letters burned. B12 Walter confesses the forgery and the interception; Nate finds the tin in the ballroom. B13 Val confronts Eleanor publicly; Nate chooses the letters; June reveals she moved the tin. B14 June hides the tin in the library; Walter distracts the guards; Nate sees the star. B15 Walter confesses the payments and forgery; Madison admits she wants the shares. B16 Nate tears the prenup; Nate and Val open the tin; Nate cuts his mother out. B17 Val, Nate, and Walter plan the public exposure; Nate interrupts the wedding; Walter names Eleanor. B18 Val reads a letter; Eleanor destroys pages; Val recovers the fake letter from the safe. B19 Val compares signatures; Eleanor tries to buy her. B20 Eleanor expels Val into the snow; Nate renounces his inheritance; Val leaves for Grand Central. B21 Nate rescues the tin from the furnace; June treats his hands; Eleanor is left alone. B22 Grand Central at 11:58; Nate arrives with the tin; the star proves the forgery; Val lets the train leave; the ornament callback.

object_ledger.name: the red cookie tin
object_ledger.description: Holds the 72 sealed letters; hidden in the library, moved to the cellar, nearly burned, rescued by Nate.

object_ledger.name: the fake letter
object_ledger.description: Eleanor's forged goodbye letter, signed Valentina Reyes but missing the star; the proof that breaks the lie.

object_ledger.name: the crystal star ornament
object_ledger.description: The gift Val gave Nate at nineteen; he keeps it, Eleanor locks it away, and Val hangs it on his coat at the end.

object_ledger.name: the prenup
object_ledger.description: Madison's contract for half of Cole Hotels; Nate tears it, and the shares become her real motive.

object_ledger.name: the old letter
object_ledger.description: One intercepted letter Walter keeps; it proves the letters reached the mansion and leads Val to the tin.
